title: How Music Takes Control of Your Body
topic: Music entrains movement, heart rate and breathing, triggers dopamine at peak moments, changes exercise and pain perception, and loops in your head
style: LOUDNESS: showreel grammar, one motion discipline per shot, every visual driven by the real soundtrack (per-frame band analysis). Ink #0D0716, magenta #FF2E88, lime #C6FF3D, cyan #33E1FF, cream #FFF4E6, violet #7B5CFF. The score itself demonstrates each claim: tempo ramp, true silence, then a drop. Series bug INSIDE YOU · EP 05.

narration.text: This song is changing your body right now.
Feel your foot? It's probably already tapping.
That's because your brain's movement areas fire to a beat, even when you're sitting still.
Speed up the music, and your heart rate and breathing tend to rise with it.
Stop it, and they fall. Sometimes below where they started.
And that shiver at the big moment? Your brain releases dopamine, the same reward chemical behind food and other pleasures.
Runners match their steps to the beat, and music can make exercise feel easier.
After surgery, patients who listened to music reported less pain and anxiety.
And that song stuck in your head? About nine in ten people get one every week.
Which song gives you chills? Tell me in the comments.
